name: PREVIOUSLY IN GTM
tagline: A weekly read for founders, GTM leaders and growth marketers.
title: Decide what your growth loop pays in before you build it
standfirst: A long read on the one contract term, hidden inside every invite scheme, creator programme and bonus plan, that decides whether growth compounds or fills with noise.
cover_sub: The contract term hidden inside every invite scheme, creator programme and bonus plan.

insight.label: By the numbers
insight.text: distinct ads a month, run by a single media buyer, once creators were paid on performance.
insight.source: Source: GTM Weekly #31 (Work-Bench), reporting Wispr Flow's paid growth strategy. Reported, not audited.

quote.label: Worth pinning above your desk
quote.text: Scarcity on top of a mediocre product is just friction.
quote.attribution: GTM Strategist newsletter, on Instinct's invite-only launch

framework.title: Four decisions behind every growth loop
framework.subtitle: Ask them in order.
framework.footer: The trigger is the one to argue over.

items.name: Currency
items.question: What are you handing over?
items.example: Cash, access, status, freedom from a target.

items.name: Trigger
items.question: What event releases it?
items.example: Prefer one you control or can verify, close to a closed deal.

items.name: Clock
items.question: How often is it paid?
items.example: Match your sales cycle, not the playbook you borrowed.

items.name: Ceiling
items.question: What stops it?
items.example: A cap protects budget. No cap says: more of what works.

diagram.before_label: Before: pay on an event the payee reports
diagram.before_note: The trigger is easy to inflate and the clock is slower than the creator's patience.
diagram.after_label: After: pay on a signal the payer controls
diagram.after_note: Spend only flows to ads that work, and a short clock keeps good creators paid while deals mature.
diagram.footnote: A teaching diagram, not a reported case. Wispr's terms are described in GTM Weekly #31.
